claims.text: Autocomplete is absent from the default dynamic type set but can be added through a custom typeSet. MongoDB recommends static autocomplete mappings because broad dynamic autocomplete increases index size, resource use, and scoring risks. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-24)
Index only fields needed by the search workload when their names are known. MongoDB and Mongoose recommend static mappings to reduce unnecessary index storage and resource usage. (high confidence)

Dynamic indexing of arbitrary field names can cause mapping explosions, increasing mongot memory consumption and potentially crashing it. MongoDB recommends restricting mappings or restructuring keys into a tuple-like schema. (low confidence)
Static nested-field mappings require definitions for each parent; dotted field names cannot replace that hierarchy. (low confidence)

With mappings.dynamic:true, the default type set applies. A named custom typeSet can change dynamically indexed types; document, embeddedDocuments, vector, and deprecated field types are excluded from custom type sets. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)
MongoDB recommends limiting dynamic mappings to changing or unknown fields inside a document rather than enabling them indiscriminately at the root. (low confidence)

TCGplayer’s benchmark repository keeps collection and Search mapping definitions in src/mongo_bench/resources/bench_collections.json and directs test plans to reference that file or its commit and path. Its index named bench_search_dynamic_all actually uses dynamic:false, showing why benchmark interpretation must inspect definitions rather than names. (low confidence)
Dynamic mappings automatically index supported fields, while mappings.dynamic:false with mappings.fields selects explicit fields and search types. (high confidence)
Static definitions override dynamic treatment per field. To index one field as both string and autocomplete, explicitly include both types in its static mapping array. (high confidence)

Dynamic indexing can include unnecessary fields and increase storage use. Static mappings can reduce the index footprint by restricting indexed fields; a universal query-latency improvement is not established. (high confidence)

The documented configurable dynamic syntax permits mappings.dynamic to reference a named typeSet, whose field-type configurations are defined in the top-level typeSets array. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

A static field definition can carry analyzer settings independently for each string field; Mongoose demonstrates lucene.standard, lucene.english, and lucene.keyword configurations inside mappings.fields. (low confidence)

Mongoose lets applications declare mapping JSON with schema.searchIndex() and create declared search indexes with Model.createSearchIndexes(); its examples include static typed fields and field-specific analyzers. (low confidence)

Omitting mappings.dynamic defaults to false in the mapping definition, even though MongoDB performance guidance describes the default index-creation configuration as dynamic. Set the value explicitly. (medium confidence)

Pureinsights describes MAPT experiments that supply mappings, representative data, and queries, then measure indexing and query performance under configurable concurrency. The tool was developed with MongoDB; this is methodology, not independent proof of a static-mapping speedup. (low confidence)

A Reddit author reported unchanged Artillery load-test results after replacing a smaller static mapping with a dynamic mapping on an M0 cluster. This uncontrolled observation does not establish a general latency relationship. (low confidence)

Percona Search documents dynamic mappings, including newly added supported fields, and explicit static mappings for its own MongoDB Search implementation. This corroborates mapping concepts across implementations, not a benchmark advantage. (low confidence)
